verdict.rationale: GitBook documents an official GitBook CLI under its docs-as-code section. From the shell it lets users list organizations, inspect spaces and pages, ask questions against their docs, and build and publish integrations. A community post says the CLI "is no longer under active development," but it quotes an old README for the legacy open-source book CLI, so it does not concretely contradict the current documented CLI. Missing for 10: detailed documentation of agent-oriented CLI usage (e.g. machine-readable output or agent workflows), independent or hands-on corroboration of the current CLI, and clarity on how it relates to the legacy CLI.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: list organizations, inspect spaces and pages, ask questions against your docs, and build and publish integrations — all without leaving the shell
